rationale: The compaction finding gains its normative basis: the repo's own compaction documentation states that the log grows without bound unless users compact it and shows the call on the instance, which the actor layer takes away. The account for that question is updated; nothing else changes.

interpretations.rationale: Source-only current account; no execution. The duty is the repository's own: docs/omnipaxos/compaction.md opens with 'As time passes, the replicated log in OmniPaxos will grow large. To avoid letting the log growing infinitely large, we support two ways of compaction that can be initiated by users', and its example calls `omni_paxos.trim(trim_idx)` on the instance (docs/omnipaxos/compaction.md:1-11); the core API behind that is `OmniPaxos::trim(trim_index: Option<usize>) -> Result<(), CompactionErr>` and `OmniPaxos::snapshot(compact_idx, local_only)` (omni_paxos.rs:242-262). The runtime layer removes the ability to discharge that duty: spawn_actor::<T, B, R>(op: OmniPaxos<T, B>, cfg) consumes the instance by value (handle.rs:295), the returned handle keeps only cmd_tx, events_rx, outgoing_rx, incoming_tx and decided_channel_capacity with no accessor back to the instance and no trim/snapshot method, the client protocol has no compaction request (Command is Append, AppendNotify, CurrentLeader, DecidedIdx, ReadDecidedSuffix, SubscribeDecided, Reconfigure, TryBecomeLeader, Reconnected - event.rs:90-128), and the actor never calls op.trim()/op.snapshot() (its only 'trim' is trim_oldest over its own outgoing buffer, actor.rs:239, 715-720). The layer also presents itself as the way to run the core without driving it - it removes the need to fetch and send messages manually and the actor owns that work (lib.rs:7-15) - and the shipped example uses only the handle, so nothing in the snapshot points a runtime user at the core instance instead. The comparison therefore holds as an omitted duty of the layer that owns the instance: with the layer's own documented route to bounded log growth unreachable, a runtime-only user's log can only grow. Counter-limitations kept in force: (a) the layer nowhere claims feature parity with the core, so the claim rests on the reverse direction - the documentation of the duty plus the absence of any path (three places inspected: handle methods, Command variants, actor calls into the core); (b) the consequence (unbounded log growth) is not measured, and the storage backend's behaviour when it fills - which would turn an operational issue into a write error for the actor - is not examined; (c) no source states that compaction is deliberately out of scope for the layer, and the layer does expose other core-facing operations (append, append_notify, reconfigure, read_decided_suffix, current_leader, decided_idx, try_become_leader, reconnected, subscribe_decided), so this is a specific omission rather than a policy of exposing nothing beyond writes.
limitations: Source-only account: the absence of a path is established by inspecting the handle's methods, the Command enum and the actor's calls into the core, not by an execution.
The consequence (unbounded log growth) is not measured, and the storage backend's behaviour when it fills is not examined.
No source states that compaction is deliberately out of scope for the layer; the account treats it as an omitted operation against the duty the repo's own documentation states.
